title: Delivery report field labeled expected unsettled custody aggregates collected amount instead
observed_behavior: GetDeliveryOutcomesReportAsync filters all non-settled custody rows without a date filter, counts them, then sums CollectedPiastres into DTO field UnsettledCustodyExpectedPiastres. DeliveryRules.CreateCashCustody initializes Expected to responsibility and Collected to zero; assignment persists both. RecordDeliveryResultHandler populates Collected only when Delivered and stores any variance. OwnerDashboardQueryService independently projects unsettled custody as the sum of ExpectedPiastres. The report UI binds the mismatched DTO amount. Thus an assigned/out-for-delivery order can count as unsettled while its labeled expected amount is zero; a delivered variance can also make collected differ from expected.
preconditions: At least one non-prepaid delivery has been assigned (creating Open custody) and has not yet reached Delivered, or a delivered custody has an approved recorded variance. No real runtime state was created or queried.
impact: If the DTO/UI contract means expected cash at driver risk, the report underreports that exposure while delivery is in transit and diverges from the owner dashboard. If it intentionally means cash already collected but not settled, the aggregation may be deliberate but DTO name and tests are misleading. No loss, duplicate payment, or ledger corruption is established.

independent_verification.scope: Independent challenge of coordinator report path; same baseline sources, no runtime test.

related_temporal_question: The non-settled count/amount query is global current state while delivery outcomes and settlement totals are period-filtered. DailyStatement passes a date but labels the amount “now”. Whether a historical statement should show current outstanding custody or as-of-date custody remains a separate owner policy question.
counterevidence: The application may intend this field to represent collected-but-unsettled cash; however the DTO explicitly says Expected, the existing integration assertion comments expected responsibility, and the owner dashboard uses ExpectedPiastres.
Existing reporting test checks the row only after full amount is collected, so Expected and Collected are equal in that test.
No API, SQL Server, or UI execution was performed; no current incident is known.

repair_specification.recommended_direction: Confirm report contract. Existing DTO name, owner dashboard, and test comments support ExpectedPiastres: if that is the intended meaning, sum c.ExpectedPiastres. If the intended metric is collected-but-unsettled, rename the DTO/display and retain/add a distinct expected-at-risk metric so the two values are not conflated.
tests: Open assigned COD custody before Delivered: report count is one and expected amount equals responsibility; collected amount is zero.
Delivered with exact collection: expected and collected equal and both projections agree.
Delivered with approved shortage/overage: expected remains original responsibility while collected reflects actual; report fields follow chosen names/contract.
After settlement, unsettled count/amount falls to zero; settled-period totals remain date-filtered.
Historical DailyStatement queried before/after a later settlement: assert current-now versus as-of-date policy explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: DTO field name and source aggregate express the same amount.
Owner dashboard and delivery report agree for the same non-settled custody cohort when they claim to show expected custody.
In-transit and variance cases are covered by tests; no real printer or financial operation is needed.
Historical statement temporal semantics are documented separately.
Before delivery, delivery report and owner dashboard agree on expected cash responsibility for the same open custody cohort while collected remains zero.
repair_specification.risks: Renaming DTO fields is a client wire-contract change. Switching to Expected may change displayed amount for in-transit and variance cases but does not alter ledger rows or driver settlement.
required_regression_tests: Assigned, open COD custody before delivery: query the same unsettled cohort through the delivery report and owner dashboard; assert both expected-at-risk amounts equal the original cash responsibility, collected is zero, and counts agree.

Approved variance cross-view case: expected-at-risk remains the original responsibility in both projections while collected reflects the actual driver collection; assert the chosen field names and values explicitly.
